summary: A web platform for exploring urban heat across Delhi. It combines satellite-derived land surface temperature at 30 m resolution with a trained model, so you can find hotspots and compare what-if cooling scenarios, such as more vegetation or less built-up surface.

images.caption: Overview of observed land surface temperature for a selected month

sections.title: The challenge
body: Urbanization has replaced vegetation and water with heat-absorbing surfaces, intensifying the urban heat island effect. Ground stations and city-wide policies can't show how heat differs from one block to the next, or what would cool a specific place.

routes.label: Observed heat
routes.note: The heat map shows stored satellite-derived observations, not predictions.

routes.label: Cooling scenario
routes.note: A scenario changes inputs such as NDVI or tree cover and compares two model estimates. It is a what-if estimate, not a measurement.

sections.title: What the platform does
items: Explore observed land surface temperature on a map, month by month.
Look up any location and see its temperature and environmental features.
Compare baseline and scenario estimates by changing NDVI, EVI, tree cover or built surface.
Rank the hottest cells and download a month's observations as CSV.

sections.title: Model results
sections.note: Evaluated on held-out spatial blocks, so training and test areas do not overlap. Both models met the targets (RMSE of 1.5 °C or less, R² of 0.85 or more), and XGBoost scored better.

sections.title: Limits and next steps
items: Scenario results are model estimates, not measurements or proof that an intervention causes cooling.
Not yet validated against ground-station data.
Planned: SHAP explanations for per-location drivers.
Planned: a cooling-optimization engine and more cities.
